correctness.rationale: Three independently constructed standard-library checks were replayed. All 6,545 triple and 52,360 quadruple candidates are covered by 10 and 38 S7 orbit representatives; exactly one successful 4-orbit of size 840 has explicit 20->29->35 forcing closure. Full-subset and finite-group enumerations agree. Direct combinatorial pencil/transversal moves show 13 jumps and a unique slide. Full 840-root BFS and independent transitive-root BFS agree on the 840-state, diameter-six jump metric and the 420-edge matching slide graph. Finite computations prove precisely this finite claim, not any infinite extension.

value.rationale: KG(7,3) is the first 35-vertex odd graph beyond the Petersen graph, with directly studied Fano-plane combinatorics. The classification determines a previously unsupported exact dynamic monitoring optimum (four sensors versus known ordinary dominating seven), gives a natural unique incidence-theoretic model for every optimum, and sharply separates physically local one-token sliding (420 disconnected pairs) from global reassignment (one 13-regular graph of diameter six). The exact optimal-state geometry is a reusable finite benchmark, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
